Voice recorded hospital patch:
Receiving hospital, this is Medic 53, en route with a 50-year-old male complaining of chest pain beginning around 8:00 p.m. while eating dinner. He describes constant substernal pressure radiating to his left arm, accompanied by mild nausea and sweating. Pain was initially six out of ten and is currently five out of ten. He reports that this feels similar to his previous heart attack. Relevant history includes prior myocardial infarction and congestive heart failure, and he takes warfarin. He denies shortness of breath, loss of consciousness, recent trauma, or vomiting.

Patient is alert and oriented times four, speaking in complete sentences, with unlabored breathing. Skin is mildly pale and diaphoretic, and lung sounds are clear bilaterally. Initial vitals at 9:02 p.m. were heart rate 72, blood pressure 112 over 74, oxygen saturation 99 percent on room air, respiratory rate 18, and blood glucose 120. Repeat vitals at 9:17 p.m. are heart rate 76, blood pressure 108 over 70, oxygen saturation 98 percent on room air, and pain five out of ten. Patient is positioned comfortably on the stretcher and is being reassessed during transport. No medications have been administered by our crew. Estimated arrival is eight minutes.
